challenge.better_approach: Teaching the trouble device to recheck was looked at and rejected: it would make trouble read the tester's seal store and slug rules, coupling the store's owner to every raiser. The inspector precedent (95557c2ed44f) puts the recheck with the raiser and the fold with trouble; this follows it. Clearing at seal time already exists (validation_store's round-trip clear) but fires only on a red-to-green change through the door, never for a proof deleted or a held-red whose seal went green through a different identity.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a seal-red slug maps back to at most one proof: seal_trouble_identity folds every non [a-z0-9-] run to '-', so two proofs differing only in '_' vs '-' would collide; measured 2026-11-18, no collision among the house's proofs (the measure script indexed every **/proofs/*.py).
challenge.prior_art: inspector.recheck (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py) for inspector-new-finding-*; validation_store's re-seal round-trip clear for seal-red on a red->green seal; validation_store.standing for the proven predicate.
challenge.real_collision: none: the ticket-unqueued-*/ticket-refused-* kinds are raised by cairn/machines/ticket and get their own sibling ticket at that owner (RULE 1); red-tickets-outline-check-* is out.

answers.falsifier: Done when, in a scratch world, a seal-red trouble for a proven proof and one for a proof that no longer exists are cleared by the recheck and the drain, while a seal-red for a never-sealed proof stands, and the same holds for red-tickets-held-red; wrong intent if a cleared trouble's proof was in fact red (standing() is the store's own door, so it would be the store that was wrong).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the gap measured in bin/cmd/cleanup (its one recheck step hands the inspector only inspector-new-finding-* ids) and in the 24 live troubles read 2026-11-18 on akiendelllinux; its precedent is ticket 95557c2ed44f
answers.how: The tester, which raises both kinds (validation_store's announce and red_tickets._hold, each as ModuleRaiser('tester')), gains a recheck: for each named identity it finds the proof whose seal_trouble_identity (seal-red) or slugged red_tickets:held:red:<rel> prefix (held-red) matches, and emits clear_trouble when validation_store.standing(proof)['proven'] is True or no proof file matches. It is reached through the tester's CLI (bin/cairn test --recheck-troubles <ids>), and bin/cmd/cleanup runs it as a step before the drain, the way it runs the inspector's --recheck. The trouble device's drain does the fold (Law 6).
answers.traces_to: Law 9 and Law 7: a trouble whose cause is gone, standing, is a record that no longer says what is; the clear is the trouble device's own fold of the raiser's emission (Law 6), as in ticket 95557c2ed44f.
answers.what: cairn cleanup clears the tester's seal-red-* and red-tickets-held-red-* troubles whose cause is gone: the proof is sealed green with its fingerprint matching, or the proof file no longer exists.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-18 at the Dell house: of 24 live troubles, 9 of the tester's kinds are clearable now — 7 of 7 red-tickets-held-red (each proof proven) and 2 of 4 seal-red (proof file gone); the other 2 seal-red (inferenceproxy) are really red and stay.

title: cairn cleanup clears the tester's seal-red-* and red-tickets-held-red-* troubles whose cause is gone: the proof is seale
